stories.title: Noreen Niazi moved from Lahore jail to hospital due to high blood pressure: lawyer
stories.brief: LAHORE: Incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan’s sister Noreen Niazi was moved from Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology on Wednesday due to high blood pressure, her lawyer said.

stories.title: Imran Khan’s sister Noreen taken to Punjab Institute of Cardiology after health issue in jail: lawyer
stories.brief: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan’s sister Noreen Niazi, 70, was admitted to Lahore's Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) on Wednesday following a deterioration in her health while in custody, according to her legal counsel.

stories.title: Nine terrorists killed in two intelligence-based operations in Balochistan: ISPR
stories.brief: Security forces killed nine terrorists belonging to Indian backed Fitna al-Hindustan during two Intelligence-Based Operations (IBOs) in Balochistan's Kachhi and Wadh districts, the military's media wing said on Wednesday.

stories.title: Religious scholars reaffirm fatwa against suicide attacks, terrorism
stories.brief: Religious scholars, spiritual leaders and representatives of different faiths unanimously reaffirmed the fatwa (religious ruling) against suicide attacks, terrorism, extremism and the killing of innocent people, while fully endorsing the national narrative of Paigham-e-Pakistan.

The deputy prime minister directed the relevant authorities to closely monitor market trends and ensure adequate wheat supplies across Pakistan.

stories.title: Secret to national development lies in AI and digitisation: PM Shehbaz
stories.brief: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Wednesday that the secret to national development lay in artificial intelligence (AI) and digitisation, stressing the need to accelerate their adoption across key sectors, including agriculture, trade, healthcare and governance.

stories.title: In support of One-China policy, Pakistan bans Taiwanese airlines from using its airspace: report
stories.brief: He said that Islamabad now only permitted airlines from the People’s Republic of China to fly over Pakistan, excluding Taiwan. According to flight tracking data, Taiwanese carriers began rerouting flights over the weekend, with China Airlines Ltd and Eva Airways Corp no longer flying over Pakistan since Sunday.
